Ask the host

Keep it friendly and keep these to yourselves: your budget, what you’d offer, how soon you need to move, or how much you love it. Here’s why:
  • The host usually works for the seller, so anything you say can be passed along.
  • Mentioning a budget or top price tells the seller what you can pay, and that leaves Chris less room to negotiate.
  • Sharing your timeline or that you’re in a hurry tells the seller they can hold firm on price.
  • Showing how much you love it takes away leverage. Smile, look around, and save the excitement for the car.
Chris will handle all of that for you.
  1. Why are the sellers moving, and what timing do they want for closing?
  2. It has been on the market since August. Have the sellers had any feedback?
  3. What year was the roof done, was it permitted, and is the warranty transferable?
  4. Solar: how many panels, what year, is it fully paid off with no lien, and is there a battery?
  5. Are all 5 bedrooms and any additions or enclosures permitted? Does the tax record match 5 bed / 2,336 sf?
  6. Which items stay: hot tub, washer/dryer, fridges, any furniture?
  7. Is the seller disclosure ready? Any known issues: termites, leaks, plumbing or the sewer line?

Snap a photo of any flyer or disclosure handout and text it to Chris.
